questions.prompt: In July 2024, a single software failure at CrowdStrike cost Fortune 500 companies an estimated how much in a matter of hours?
options: $5.4 billion
$540 million
$54 billion
$1.8 billion
$12.5 billion
questions.explanation: The lecture cites an estimated $5.4 billion loss for Fortune 500 companies, showing that failures of complex distributed systems are a multi-billion dollar reality that traditional testing cannot anticipate.

questions.prompt: According to the lecture, human error contributes to what share of preventable incidents?
questions.explanation: The Hurricane Sandy slide states that human error contributes to 79% of preventable incidents; 43.3% is Amazon's reported decrease in SLA violations after GameDays.

questions.prompt: Which sequence matches the timeline of Netflix's chaos engineering origin story?
options: 2008 database corruption, 2010 Chaos Monkey created, 2011 Simian Army announced, 2012 open-sourced
2008 database corruption, 2010 Simian Army announced, 2011 Chaos Monkey created, 2012 open-sourced
2008 Chaos Monkey created, 2010 database corruption, 2011 Simian Army announced, 2012 open-sourced
2008 database corruption, 2010 Chaos Monkey open-sourced, 2011 Simian Army announced, 2012 Chaos Kong created
2006 database corruption, 2008 Chaos Monkey created, 2010 Simian Army announced, 2012 open-sourced
questions.explanation: After the August 2008 database corruption halted DVD shipping for three days, Netflix created Chaos Monkey in 2010, announced the Simian Army in 2011 and open-sourced it in 2012.

questions.prompt: Which Simian Army tool simulates the failure of an entire AWS Availability Zone?
options: Chaos Gorilla
Chaos Kong
Chaos Monkey
Latency Monkey
Security Monkey
questions.explanation: Chaos Gorilla simulates the loss of a whole AWS Availability Zone; Chaos Kong goes a step further and simulates a full AWS region failure.

questions.prompt: A team wants to check that its services stay resilient when network communication becomes slow rather than failing outright. Which Simian Army tool is designed for this?
options: Latency Monkey
Chaos Monkey
Chaos Gorilla
Security Monkey
Chaos Kong
questions.explanation: Latency Monkey injects artificial delays to test resilience to network degradation; Chaos Monkey instead randomly terminates production instances to test survival of instance loss.

questions.prompt: How does principlesofchaos.org define Chaos Engineering?
options: Experimenting on a system to build confidence that it can withstand turbulent conditions in production
Testing a system before release to prove that it contains no defects under turbulent conditions
Load testing a system to find the maximum traffic it can handle before it crashes in production
Randomly breaking production systems without any hypothesis to see how users are affected
Simulating attacks on a system to find security vulnerabilities before they reach production
questions.explanation: The quoted definition is experimenting on a system to build confidence in its capability to withstand turbulent conditions in production; the lecture also describes it as a hypothesis-driven, scientific practice.

questions.prompt: In the fourth and final step of a chaos experiment, "Disprove Hypothesis", what do engineers do?
options: Systematically look for differences between the control and experimental groups to find weaknesses
Establish a measurable baseline of normal system behavior before anything is changed
Predict that the steady state will continue in both the control and experimental groups
Inject real-world failure events such as server crashes, network partitions and CPU spikes
Restore every terminated instance and confirm that the hypothesis has been proven true
questions.explanation: Disproving the hypothesis means searching for differences between the control and experimental groups to expose weaknesses; defining a baseline, predicting that steady state continues and injecting failures are steps 1, 2 and 3.

questions.prompt: In the lecture's payment-microservice example, which statement is the steady state hypothesis?
options: Under normal load, the checkout service keeps p99 latency under 200ms and an error rate below 0.1%
Terminate 30% of the checkout service instances while the service is handling normal load
Auto-scaling and load balancing restore the checkout service within 30 seconds of the failure
The checkout service must never fail, no matter how many of its instances are terminated
Inject real-world failure events into the checkout service and then record its error rate
questions.explanation: A steady state hypothesis is a measurable, quantifiable description of normal behavior (p99 latency under 200ms, error rate below 0.1%); terminating 30% of instances is the experiment, and recovery within 30 seconds is the expected result.

questions.prompt: A team is ready to run its first chaos experiment in production. Following the principle of minimizing the blast radius, which target should it start with?
options: A single container
An entire service
One Availability Zone
A full AWS region
Every pod in the cluster
questions.explanation: The blast radius grows from container to instance/pod, service, Availability Zone and region, and teams should begin with the smallest possible blast radius in production, so a single container comes first.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of automated stop conditions (circuit breakers) in chaos experiments?
options: To halt an experiment if the system deviates too far from steady state
To randomly terminate production instances during an experiment
To widen the blast radius automatically after each successful run
To move an experiment from production back into a staging environment
To measure how long the system runs before its next failure occurs
questions.explanation: Circuit breakers are a control mechanism for the blast radius: they automatically stop an experiment when the system strays too far from its steady state.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the modern chaos engineering toolkit (2023-2025) is correct?
options: LitmusChaos is a CNCF project best suited to Kubernetes environments
Gremlin is a CNCF project with native Kubernetes (K8s) integration
Chaos Monkey is a commercial SaaS tool aimed at enterprise adoption
AWS FIS is an open-source tool known as the original chaos tool
Azure Chaos Studio is a commercial SaaS tool known for GameDays
questions.explanation: LitmusChaos is the CNCF project with native K8s integration; Gremlin is the commercial SaaS tool known for being user-friendly and for GameDays, while Chaos Monkey is the original open-source tool.

questions.prompt: A service runs on average 200 hours before it fails and then takes on average 2 hours to restore. Using the formula from the lecture, what is its MTBF?
options: 202 hours
198 hours
200 hours
100 hours
400 hours
questions.explanation: MTBF = MTTF + MTTR, so 200 hours + 2 hours = 202 hours; 200 hours on its own is only the MTTF.

questions.prompt: Which resilience metric answers the question "How long can a system be expected to run before it fails?"
options: MTTF (Mean Time to Failure)
MTTR (Mean Time to Recovery)
MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures)
p99 latency
Error rate
questions.explanation: MTTF measures how long a system runs before it fails; MTTR measures how quickly service is restored after a failure, and MTBF is the total time from one failure to the next.

questions.prompt: According to the industry benchmark for MTTR given in the lecture, elite teams restore service in under how much time?
options: 5 minutes
30 minutes
30 seconds
60 minutes
15 minutes
questions.explanation: The benchmark is under 30 minutes for top teams and under 5 minutes for elite teams.

questions.prompt: A system offering 99.99% availability ("four nines") allows approximately how much downtime per year?
options: 52.56 minutes
8.76 hours
5.26 minutes
4.4 minutes
44 minutes
questions.explanation: Four nines means 52.56 minutes of annual downtime (about 4.4 minutes per month); 8.76 hours per year corresponds to three nines and 5.26 minutes to five nines.

questions.prompt: What key result did Amazon report after implementing GameDays?
options: A 43.3% decrease in SLA violations
A 79% decrease in preventable incidents
A 43.3% decrease in mean time to recovery
A 50% decrease in deployment failures
A 30% decrease in p99 latency
questions.explanation: Amazon's dedicated 2-4 hour GameDay periods led to a 43.3% decrease in SLA violations; 79% is the share of preventable incidents attributed to human error.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes Google's DiRT (Disaster Recovery Testing) program from the other industry approaches described in the lecture?
options: It goes beyond technology to test business processes and human response
It runs automated chaos experiments continuously in production
It sets aside dedicated 2-4 hour periods for teams to run experiments
It randomly terminates production instances to test instance loss
It provides native Kubernetes integration as a CNCF project
questions.explanation: DiRT, founded in 2006 by Site Reliability Engineers, also tests business processes and human response; continuous automated chaos in production describes Netflix, and 2-4 hour periods describe Amazon's GameDays.

questions.prompt: In the Honeycomb case study on an AWS Availability Zone failure, when did the team intentionally run its production experiment?
options: During peak traffic, for a realistic test
During off-peak hours, to avoid customer impact
During a maintenance window, with users logged out
Before any staging tests, to save rollout time
Only after a real AZ outage, to confirm the cause
questions.explanation: Honeycomb ran staging tests first, then progressed to production and intentionally ran the experiment during peak traffic for a realistic test, terminating a third of its 'Shepherd' pods with zero customer impact.

questions.prompt: Which statement reflects the core principles of resilient engineering presented in the lecture?
options: Reducing MTTR is often more valuable than trying to prevent all failures
Preventing all failures is more valuable than reducing recovery time
Experiments should start with the largest blast radius to learn the most
Technical tools alone are enough; no cultural change is required
Experiments should stay manual and separate from the CI/CD pipeline
questions.explanation: The lecture states that reducing MTTR is often more valuable than trying to prevent all failures; it also says to start with a small blast radius, pair tools with cultural transformation and automate experiments in CI/CD.
